title: Geodesic Domes: The Wave of the Future That Wasn't
summary: Josh and Chuck explore geodesic domes: their appeal and drawbacks as houses, the 1920s Zeiss planetarium in Jena, Germany (Walther Bauersfeld) as the first, and R. Buckminster Fuller's patent and promotion of them as the "house of the future." They cover the geometry (triangles, icosahedron, tensegrity, vector equilibrium), the Ford Rotunda dome in Dearborn, Michigan (built by Fuller, burned in 1953 during Christmas decorating and waterproofing work), Fuller's Manhattan dome proposal, the Montreal Expo 67 dome, and famous domes such as Epcot's Spaceship Earth, the Eden Project in Cornwall, the Tacoma Dome, and the Fukuoka Yahoo! Dome. They also discuss practical pros and cons (heating efficiency, wind resistance, hurricane survival, furniture fit, leaks at seams). The episode ends with listener mail from Veronica in Indianapolis.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and personal taste in homes
segments.summary: Hosts joke around about word pronunciation and say they are not fans of geodesic domes aesthetically, comparing them with craftsman bungalows and mid-century modern homes.

segments.title: Bauersfeld's Zeiss planetarium and the first geodesic dome
segments.summary: Zeiss wanted a planetarium in Jena, Germany, and Walther Bauersfeld designed what is widely cited as the first geodesic dome. It was light, held many people, and kicked off a planetarium craze.

segments.title: Buckminster Fuller, the patent, and nature-inspired design
segments.summary: Richard Buckminster Fuller patented the geodesic dome and promoted it as the house of the future, citing large interior volume with little material and lightweight strength, and drawing on natural forms.

segments.title: Geometry of the dome: triangles, icosahedron, and tensegrity
segments.summary: Fuller found that packed spheres formed triangles and squares; dividing triangles into smaller ones and curving them yields a near-sphere based on an icosahedron. Triangles are not all the same size. Fuller coined the term tensegrity (tensional integrity). Chuck and Josh discuss geometry class and triangle strength as with bridge trusses.

segments.title: Why geodesic domes are strong: force distribution and Epcot's Spaceship Earth
segments.summary: Force applied to a triangle frame spreads across the structure, making domes strong. Vector equilibrium balances gravity and circumferential forces. The Epcot dome is built of pyramids and sheds rain via grooves into lagoons. Discussion of Epcot's rides.

segments.title: Ford Rotunda dome and its 1953 fire
segments.summary: Ford Motor Company asked Fuller to enclose the Dearborn rotunda courtyard, and his dome was built below cost. The dome burned in a fire caused by vapors from heated waterproofing sealer ignited by a propane heater while Christmas decorations were being set up below. The whole building was lost.

segments.title: Expo 67 and the Manhattan dome proposal
segments.summary: Fuller's dome at the Montreal Expo 67 and his proposal to enclose part of Manhattan under a dome, with claimed climate control and snow removal savings. Hosts raise problems such as smell and sewer gas.

segments.title: Pros and cons of living in geodesic domes
segments.summary: Advantages include heating and cooling efficiency, wind resistance, and hurricane survival. Disadvantages include noise and smell travel, privacy, furniture and fixtures designed for rectangles, and wasted space and lack of wall anchors. Leaks at seams and nodes are a major problem.

segments.title: Famous domes: Tacoma, Fukuoka Yahoo Dome, Eden Project
segments.summary: Discussion of the Tacoma Dome, the retractable Fukuoka Yahoo! Dome baseball stadium, and the Eden Project biomes in Cornwall. Also a tangent about sports team moves.

segments.title: Spaceship Earth name, Walt Disney, and the Fuller essay
segments.summary: Epcot stands for Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow; Spaceship Earth was influenced by Fuller and named after his essay Operating Manual for Spaceship Earth. Hosts discuss a rumor about Walt Disney's signature.

segments.title: Listener mail from Veronica
segments.summary: Veronica from Indianapolis writes in about listening to the show and asks for a tour stop in Indianapolis. Hosts respond about future tour cities and mention a birthday congratulation.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close with how to contact the show and the website links.
